provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original task the input holds two equal panels side by side. A full-height divider column of colour 4 sits exactly in the middle. The left panel uses 6 on background 0 and the right panel uses 8 on 0. The output is the cellwise union of the two panels, with the panels aligned by translation: a cell is 2 if either panel is non-background there, otherwise 0. Every D4 transform maps both panels the same way, so in visible coordinates the output is still the cellwise union of two translated panels. Only the divider's orientation changes. Rotating by 90 or 270 degrees (d4%4 in {1,3}) turns the divider column into a middle row. Rotating by 0 or 180 degrees, with or without the row reflection, keeps it a middle column. The emitted program slices the two panels directly from the visible grid on either side of the divider: top/bottom for a row, left/right for a column. It marks every cell where either panel differs from palette[0] with palette[2]. The divider is taken as the exact middle line filled entirely with palette[4]. The program falls back to the middle line if no such line is found. Because of the exact-middle test, a panel line that happens to be uniformly coloured (e.g. a column of all 6s) can never be mistaken for the divider.
draft_notes.limitations: Panel cells are detected as 'not palette[0]', not by matching palette[6] or palette[8] exactly. This is equivalent within the generator's domain. If the two halves differ in size (impossible under the constructor), the program crops both to their common shape. The demonstrations are not used, since the axis and colour roles follow fully from d4 and palette. No constructor defects or fixture contradictions were found. The fixtures match the uniform union rule.
draft_notes.host_review: Reject proposed nonempty-only constructor narrowing. Retain blank panels and original native pair distribution. Require observed union-paint colour only when a query has a nonempty union. Blank-only queries remain allowed. Query labels are not consumed.
draft_notes.semantic_draft_review: Subscription Opus 5.5 semantic-repairs-v2 reviewed; constructor changes not applied.
